questions.q: Define frequency and state its unit. How does frequency affect pitch?
questions.a: Frequency is the number of oscillations (or compressions) per second. Its unit is hertz (Hz). Higher frequency means higher pitch (e.g., a whistle at 2000 Hz is higher-pitched than a drum at 100 Hz). Lower frequency means lower pitch. A wrong answer (e.g., "frequency is how fast sound travels") confuses frequency with speed — frequency is oscillations per second, not distance per second.

questions.q: Define amplitude and explain how it affects loudness.
questions.a: Amplitude is the maximum displacement of particles from their rest position during vibration. Greater amplitude means louder sound (more energy). Smaller amplitude means quieter sound. Amplitude does not affect pitch — a loud and quiet sound can have the same frequency. A wrong answer (e.g., "amplitude is the height of the wave") is partially correct but must connect to loudness — amplitude determines loudness, not just "height."

questions.q: State the relationship between speed, frequency, and wavelength. If a sound has frequency 340 Hz and speed 340 m/s, what is its wavelength?
questions.a: Speed = frequency * wavelength (v = f * lambda). So lambda = v/f = 340/340 = 1 m. The wavelength is 1 meter. A wrong answer (e.g., lambda = f/v = 340/340 = 1) happens to give the same number but uses the wrong formula — the correct relationship is v = f * lambda, so lambda = v/f.

questions.q: Define time period and state its relationship to frequency.
questions.a: Time period (T) is the time for one complete oscillation. Its unit is seconds. Relationship: T = 1/f, where f is frequency. If f = 50 Hz, T = 1/50 = 0.02 s. A wrong answer (e.g., "T = f") inverts the relationship — period is the reciprocal of frequency, not equal to it.

questions.q: A sound wave has frequency 500 Hz and speed 340 m/s. Calculate its wavelength and time period.
questions.a: Wavelength: lambda = v/f = 340/500 = 0.68 m. Time period: T = 1/f = 1/500 = 0.002 s. A wrong answer (e.g., lambda = 500/340) inverts the formula — lambda = v/f, not f/v.

questions.q: A student says: "Higher amplitude means higher pitch." Evaluate this statement and correct it.
questions.a: The statement is incorrect. Amplitude determines loudness, not pitch. Frequency determines pitch. A high-amplitude, low-frequency sound (loud drum) is low-pitched but loud. A low-amplitude, high-frequency sound (quiet whistle) is high-pitched but quiet. The correct statement: "Higher amplitude means louder sound; higher frequency means higher pitch." A wrong evaluation (agreeing with the student) confuses amplitude (loudness) with frequency (pitch).
